QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_6

question.text: A 'Zero Coupon Zero Principal Instrument' (ZCZP) issued by an NPO on the SSE is characterised by which of the following features?

answer.text: Fixed 4-8% coupon paid annually and principal redeemed at maturity, with an additional social-impact certification.
Variable coupon linked to SROI ratio, with principal preservation guaranteed by SEBI.
Principal-only instrument with zero coupon, redeemed at face value on maturity.
No coupon and no principal repayment at maturity; the instrument is written off the investee's books at maturity after delivering promised social impact.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook pp.69-70, ZCZP instruments are issued without any coupon and no principal is payable at maturity; the instrument is written off the investee's books at maturity after the promised social impact is delivered. The 'return' to the funder is the social impact itself. The Trap: Option A imports bond-like coupon and principal cash flows that ZCZPs do not have. Option B mixes SROI (a measurement concept) with instrument mechanics and incorrectly asserts a SEBI principal-preservation guarantee. Option C describes a principal-only redemption (a zero-coupon bond), which is the opposite of a ZCZP. Note: The defining ZCZP feature is the absence of both coupon and principal redemption — neither cash flow accrues to the investor.
